title: Accounts Payable Assistant
company: Hays Specialist Recruitment Limited - Agency - Permanent
description:
Your new companyHays are pleased to be recruiting for an Accounts Payable Administrator to join a well-established and fast-paced finance team. This is an excellent opportunity for an experienced Accounts Payable professional who enjoys working in a collaborative environment and contributing to the efficient delivery of key financial processes.
Your new roleWorking as part of a high-performing team, you will play a key role in ensuring supplier transactions are processed accurately and efficiently, supporting the smooth day-to-day operation of the purchase ledger function.
Key Responsibilities
- Processing supplier invoices and credit notes in a timely and accurate manner
- Managing supplier and internal queries, providing a professional and responsive service
- Performing supplier statement reconciliations
- Investigating and resolving accounts payable discrepancies and outstanding queries
- Maintaining accurate supplier accounts, ensuring balances are regularly reviewed and cleared where appropriate
- Closing and maintaining purchase orders within the system
- Supporting the wider finance team with additional administrative and project-related tasks as required

What you'll need to succeed
- Previous Accounts Payable experience gained within a large or complex organisation
- Strong IT skills, including proficiency in Microsoft Office applications
- Excellent communication and interpersonal skills
- A customer-focused approach with the ability to build positive relationships with stakeholders
- The ability to work effectively within a collaborative team environment
- Experience using Workday or AI-enabled finance systems would be advantageous.
- Fluent English language skills

What you'll get in returnIn return, you will receive a competitive benefits package, including:
Monday to Friday, flexible working hours with the ability to start between 7:00am-10:00am and finish between 2.30pm - 6:00pm.
- 20 days annual leave plus bank holidays
- Monday to Friday 37.5hours per week
- Additional holiday entitlement based on length of service, with the opportunity to earn up to an extra week's leave after five years
- Free on-site parking
- A supportive and inclusive team culture with regular recognition initiatives
- Comfortable communal areas for breaks and social interaction

This is a fantastic opportunity to join a stable and friendly organisation that values teamwork, professional development and employee wellbeing.

What you need to do now
If you're interested in this role, click 'apply now' to forward an up-to-date copy of your CV, or call us now.
If this job isn't quite right for you, but you are looking for a new position, please contact us for a confidential discussion about your career.

title: Credit Controller
description:
Credit Controller
Location: Rochdale
Salary: £28,000 - £32,000 per annum
Hours: Monday to Friday - 35 hours per week
Contract: Permanent, Full Time
Working Pattern: Office Based

Client Details

We are looking for an experienced and proactive Credit Controller to join a growing team based in Rochdale.

As a Credit Controller, you will support the day-to-day Credit Control function, helping to ensure outstanding debts are managed effectively and payments are received on time.

Description

The key responsibilities of a Credit Controller will be:
- Assisting with the management of a shared inbox and providing day-to-day support to the Credit Control function.
- Assessing client credit status and ensuring appropriate credit limits are set and maintained.
- Proactively managing overdue accounts and carrying out effective debt recovery procedures.
- Following up with customers regarding outstanding payments and resolving queries where required.
- Building and maintaining positive customer relationships to support timely payment and ongoing business.
- Producing regular reports on receivables, outstanding debts and overdue accounts for senior management.
- Working closely with the wider finance team to support cash flow forecasting and minimise credit risk.
- Maintaining accurate records and ensuring all credit control activity is completed efficiently and in a timely manner.

Profile

A successful Credit Controller will have:
- Previous experience in credit control or accounts receivable.
- A self-motivated and proactive approach.
- Strong written and verbal communication skills.
- Excellent problem-solving abilities.
- Strong numerical skills with excellent attention to detail and accuracy.
- Confident using Microsoft Excel
- The ability to work effectively as part of a team while also working independently.
- Excellent organisation and time management skills.
- The ability to manage multiple priorities and meet deadlines.

Job Offer
- £28,000 - £32,000 salary
- Generous annual leave
- Free on-site parking
- Discounted health plan available
- Company discounts
- Permanent, full-time employment
- 35 hours per week
- A supportive office-based working environment

Please send your CV for immediate consideration!
